Methods for fitted ZISAR models

Source: R/methods.R
zisar-methods.Rd

Standard accessors for objects returned by zisar() and zisar_fit().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'zisar'
coef(object, model = c("full", "count", "zero"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zisar'
vcov(object, model = c("full", "count", "zero"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zisar'
logLik(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zisar'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zisar'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zisar'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zisar'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.zisar'
print(
  x,
  digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L),
  signif.stars = getOption("show.signif.stars"),
  ...
)

Arguments

object, x

A fitted "zisar" object.

model

Which coefficients: "full" (count, zero-inflation, \(\rho\) and, with a spatial inflation predictor, \(\rho_0\)), "count" or "zero".

...

Not used.

digits

Number of significant digits to print.

signif.stars

Logical: show significance stars? See stats::printCoefmat().

Value

coef() a named vector, vcov() a matrix, logLik() an object of class "logLik", nobs() the number of spatial units, fitted() the fitted means \(E[y_i] = (1 - \pi_i)\mu_i\), summary() an object of class "summary.zisar".

Details

coef() and vcov() cover the regression coefficients and \(\rho\) (and \(\rho_0\) when the inflation predictor has a field or a filter); the negative binomial shape \(\kappa\) and the standard deviations \(\sigma\) and \(\sigma_0\) are reported by summary() and stored in object$kappa, object$sigma and object$sigma0. The covariance of \(\rho\) and \(\rho_0\) comes from the delta method; rows and columns of parameters held fixed are NA.

logLik() returns the Laplace-approximated marginal log-likelihood, with degrees of freedom equal to the number of estimated parameters, so stats::AIC() and stats::BIC() work on fitted models.

Examples

set.seed(1)
sim <- rzisar(10, beta = c(1, 0.5), rho = 0.4, gamma = c(-1, 0.8))
fit <- zisar(y ~ x1 | z1, data = sim$data, W = sim$W)
coef(fit)
#> count_(Intercept)          count_x1  zero_(Intercept)           zero_z1 
#>         1.3106852         0.3799217        -1.0502858         0.6185275 
#>               rho 
#>         0.2311040 
sqrt(diag(vcov(fit)))
#> count_(Intercept)          count_x1  zero_(Intercept)           zero_z1 
#>         0.8153926         0.1574565         0.4006161         0.3067666 
#>               rho 
#>         0.4686404 
AIC(fit)
#> [1] 517.8555
